summary.headline: IndiGo posted a Q4 FY26 net loss of 25.4 billion rupees, driven by 48.2 billion rupees of FX losses; FY26 underlying profit ex-FX and exceptionals was 75 billion rupees.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was hit by the December operational disruption tail, a March demand break from Middle East escalation, and a sharp rupee depreciation of about 5% in the quarter. Total income for the quarter was about 238 billion rupees (up about 3%), and EBITDAR ex-FX was 64.4 billion rupees at a 28.7% margin versus 31.0% a year earlier. Q4 capacity growth slowed to 3% (about 10% in Jan-Feb) and PRASK fell 4% to 4.46 rupees. Management guided to a mid-teens PRASK increase for Q1 FY27 on fuel charges and a low base, but flagged higher costs and a seasonally softer period from mid-June, with capacity recalibration planned.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Expected to absorb most redeployed capacity in Q1 FY27 (metro, new airports Navi Mumbai and Jewar, and leisure markets); management says domestic fuel pass-through is largely matched by yield due to government and OMC support (fuel up only 25-30% vs over 100% internationally).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Middle East and Europe were about 18% of capacity (around 160 daily flights); flights cancelled after the 28 Feb crisis, ramped to about 20s per day in March, and now about two-thirds of the 160 are operating, with full capacity targeted by end-June. International fuel charges pass through only partially.

segments.name: Fleet and network
segments.commentary: Fleet of 441 aircraft at FY26 end after 72 gross additions (51 owned-order, 21 damp-leased) and 65 redeliveries; 97 domestic and 45 international destinations; first A321 XLR inducted, deployed on Athens and Istanbul.

segments.name: Loyalty (BluChip)
segments.commentary: More than 11 million registered members; co-brand partners include SBI Cards, Kotak, Axis and IDFC First Bank; asset-light programme.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 capacity expected up around 3-4% YoY, with domestic-heavy mix as Middle East capacity ramps back.
Q1 FY27 PRASK (all-in, including fuel charge) guided to a mid-teens % increase YoY on April-May booking and pricing trends, off a low base.
CASK ex-fuel ex-FX guided to mid- to high-single-digit increase (previously mid-single-digit), dependent on utilisation and rupee.
Measured capacity optimisation from mid-June: returning damp-leased narrowbodies, reducing older CEO-generation fleet use and route recalibration; discussions with widebody ACMI partner.
No dividend recommended for FY26; no full-year ASK guidance given.
Pratt & Whitney AOG groundings in the 40s, expected to trend to the 30s by year-end; no OEM guidance beyond that.
capex_capacity: FY26 fleet: 51 aircraft inducted from original orderbook plus 21 damp-leased; 37 original-orderbook and 28 damp-lease redeliveries; fleet 441 at FY26 end.
No change to delivery schedule from the order book; flexibility is via damp-lease returns and older-technology aircraft.
Prepaid aircraft loans for 17 aircraft; 36 aircraft now unencumbered (book value above 95 billion rupees); 53 aircraft on finance leases with underlying ownership.

Capital investment of USD 820 million in GIFT City entity for aviation asset acquisition; further USD 450 million (43.4 billion rupees) prepayment of finance-lease obligations towards GIFT City entity.
Integrated Corporate Campus announced as a long-term investment.
demand_pricing: FY26 passengers above 123 million (highest ever); seat growth about 5%, passengers up about 4%, ASK growth 9.5%, RPK growth 7.5%.
Q4 demand: January residual December impact, February stabilised, March hit by Middle East escalation; April soft, May stronger per management.
Fares sticking; management says market currently inelastic to fare hikes, pricing managed daily.
Fuel: Singapore jet fuel up more than 100 points; domestic ATF increase about 25-30% after government and OMC support; Q4 fuel CASK down around 5% YoY with a one-month lag.
Q4 CASK ex-fuel ex-FX 3.15 rupees, up around 7% YoY (rupee-driven dollar costs, low utilisation, annual contractual increases).
Corporate travel: no softness seen per management; April soft, May stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Are fares fully passing through cost pressures, domestic versus international, and what is the international utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic fuel pass-through is largely recovered; international fuel is at market prices and only partly passed through via a fuel charge. International load factors were low in March and April, improving in May; no firm standalone international load-factor figure given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the mid-teens PRASK growth is base effect versus demand strength?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY26 May was extremely weak due to Pahalgam-related disruption, so the base is low; May demand is positive, and PRASK reflects both yield and load factor.

qa_highlights.question: Will fleet deliveries change?
qa_highlights.answer: No change to deliveries; near-term flexing via returning damp leases (narrowbodies) and reducing older CEO-generation aircraft given fuel burn.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CASK ex-fuel ex-FX outlook and rupee sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance moved to mid- to high-single digit increase. FX sensitivity is still about 900 million rupees per 1 rupee move; net dollar exposure about 10 billion rupees, with about 1.3 billion rupees hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging policy change given rupee volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge ceiling raised from $1 billion to $3 billion: $1 billion for 12-month cash flows and $2 billion over 2 to 5 years; hedged position currently $1.3 billion. Fuel hedging is at an early internal-deliberation stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Reversal of accruals for leadership payouts; year-on-year cost growth in line with normalised inflation and salary increases.

risks_watch: Fuel prices and the ATF pass-through: government and OMC relief is partial, and management is still negotiating with the Ministry of Petroleum on lower VAT pass-through.
Rupee: each 1 rupee move against the dollar is about 900 million rupees of mark-to-market impact; CASK ex-fuel ex-FX headwind will build as FX costs flow through.
Middle East route recovery: about two-thirds of 160 daily flights back; full capacity targeted by end-June, subject to risk assessment.
Seasonally softer demand from mid-June plus elevated fuel could pressure Q2 yields and load factors.
Pratt & Whitney groundings in the 40s; no OEM guidance beyond the 30s by year-end.
Leadership transition: Willie Walsh joins as CEO from early August 2026.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the near term, with repeated caveats that guidance is directional and volatile. Management was confident on May demand, pricing power and balance-sheet strength, and deflected on international-specific load factors and Air India comparisons.
